:
: So you're using the Internet to defend the "anti-techno" words of the
: Unabomber. The irony is a little thick in here!

Thanks for showing the world that you are well enough trained by the
media to parrot the dislike for the Manifesto while not taking a second
from your "busy" materialistic and extertainment based existence to read it.

 202. It would be hopeless for revolutionaries to try to attack the system
 without using SOME modern technology.  If nothing else they must use the
 commucation media to spread their message.  But they should use modern
 technology for only ONE purpose: to attack the technological system.

Back to the original point of this thread - maybe the media uses the word
"rambling" to hype up a story and make the author seem crazy, but yet the
average person is shielded from the author's "crazy" ideas and the status
quo can continue?  If everything else in news is exaggeration and play
acting then why not this also?  Someone who puts a ball through a hoop is
a hero, but someone who wants to make life meaningful and save us from a
stupid future is called a threat.  Thusly,

 96. ...To make an impression on society wiith words isi therefore almost
 impossible.  Take us (FC) for example.  If we had never done anything
 violent and had submitted the present writings to a publisher, they
 probably would not have been accepted.  If they had been accepted and
 published, they probably would not have attracted many readers, because
 it's more fun to watch the entertainment put out by the media than to
 read a sober essay.  Even if these writings had had many readers, most of
 these readers would soon have forgotten what they had read as their minds
 were flooded by the mass of material to which the media expose them.  In
 order to get our message before the public with some chance of making a
 lasting impresssion, we've had to kill people.

I think the Maniifesto is still too early.  There's no reason to think
that people in rich countries would have an interest in it because 
plastic gadgets and cheap entertainment are plentiful and there are
no direct glaring effects from the lifestyle of consumption and waste.
So people are happy to watch TV and life in predictable and unfulfilling
and don't really want anything more meaningful for the most part.  But
as soon as that opium-like hapiness starts to break down, people will
start looking for real answers and won't get that from this society in
denial and will never get it from the media whores who would be excluded
entirely from the solution.
